Export the Derivation Graph to a Portable Text Format

Source: R/trace_graph_export.R
export_trace_graph.Rd

Serializes the derivation graph behind trace_chains() and trace_impact() to a portable text format: Graphviz DOT, Mermaid, or GraphML. Unlike plot_trace_graph(), which needs igraph and only renders interactively, this writes the graph as text that can be committed to version control, embedded in an ADRG or vignette, rendered by Graphviz, or opened in a graph editor such as yEd.

Usage

export_trace_graph(
  trace_model,
  format = c("dot", "mermaid", "graphml"),
  adam_derivations = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  include_isolated = TRUE
)

Arguments

trace_model

A trace_model from build_trace_model().

format

One of "dot" (Graphviz), "mermaid", or "graphml".

adam_derivations

Optional data.frame of ADaM-to-ADaM derivations with columns from_dataset, from_var, to_dataset, to_var, as in trace_chains().

file

Optional output file path. When supplied, the serialized graph is written there and the text is returned invisibly; otherwise the text is returned (a single string, one line per \n).

include_isolated

Logical; when TRUE (the default) variable nodes with no derivation edge are included as isolated nodes. When FALSE only nodes that take part in at least one edge are emitted.

Value

A length-one character string containing the serialized graph, returned invisibly when file is supplied.

Details

Nodes are ADaM and SDTM variables; a directed edge runs from a derived variable to its source (A -> B reads "A is derived from B"), the same direction used throughout the engine. ADaM-to-SDTM links come from the trace model's mapping edges; ADaM-to-ADaM links are added when supplied through adam_derivations, exactly as in trace_chains(). Every variable node in the model is emitted, so orphan ADaM variables (no outgoing edge) and unused SDTM sources (no incoming edge) appear as isolated nodes unless include_isolated = FALSE. Node roles are recorded so a renderer can colour ADaM and SDTM variables differently. This is a pure serialization: it does not change trace levels, coverage, or any scoring.

See also

plot_trace_graph() for interactive plotting with igraph, trace_chains() for the graph model itself.

Examples

adam <- data.frame(
  dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"), variable = c("AGE", "AAGE"),
  label = c("Age", "Analysis Age")
)
sdtm <- data.frame(dataset = "DM", variable = "AGE", label = "Age")
map <- data.frame(
  adam_dataset = "ADSL", adam_var = "AGE",
  sdtm_domain = "DM", sdtm_var = "AGE", confidence = 1
)
tm <- build_trace_model(adam, sdtm, mapping = map)
deriv <- data.frame(
  from_dataset = "ADAE", from_var = "AAGE",
  to_dataset = "ADSL", to_var = "AGE"
)

# Graphviz DOT
cat(export_trace_graph(tm, "dot", adam_derivations = deriv))
#> digraph trace {
#>   rankdir=LR;
#>   node [fontname="Helvetica"];
#>   n1 [label="ADSL.AGE", fillcolor="#2C6DB5", style=filled, shape=box];
#>   n2 [label="ADAE.AAGE", fillcolor="#2C6DB5", style=filled, shape=box];
#>   n3 [label="DM.AGE", fillcolor="#F39C12", style=filled, shape=box];
#>   n1 -> n3;
#>   n2 -> n1;
#> }

# Mermaid, for a Markdown document
cat(export_trace_graph(tm, "mermaid", adam_derivations = deriv))
#> flowchart LR
#>   n1["ADSL.AGE"]
#>   n2["ADAE.AAGE"]
#>   n3["DM.AGE"]
#>   n1 --> n3
#>   n2 --> n1
#>   classDef adam fill:#2C6DB5,stroke:#1b4a7a,color:#ffffff;
#>   classDef sdtm fill:#F39C12,stroke:#9a6207,color:#ffffff;
#>   class n1,n2 adam;
#>   class n3 sdtm;
